inspiration.observed_pattern: Multiple staged match sources are combined with UNION ALL, ranked per lookup key so the earliest stage wins, and then left-joined to a larger result while preserving unmatched rows.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: The fixture independently models product-code resolution from exact and alias candidate tables, uses ROW_NUMBER to choose the deterministic highest-priority match, and LEFT JOINs the chosen result to every catalog item without copying source schema or application context.

fixture_notes: Exact candidates outrank aliases for item 1; item 2 has only an alias candidate; item 3 remains NULL-extended because it has no candidate.
determinism_notes: Fixed item IDs, candidate stages, and supplier codes define both ranking and final order; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE catalog_items (item_id INT PRIMARY KEY, item_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE exact_item_matches (item_id INT NOT NULL, supplier_code VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE alias_item_matches (item_id INT NOT NULL, supplier_code VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)
INSERT INTO catalog_items VALUES (1, 'red mug'), (2, 'blue bowl'), (3, 'green plate')

steps.sql: WITH ranked_matches AS (SELECT item_id, supplier_code, match_stage, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY item_id ORDER BY match_stage, supplier_code) AS match_rank FROM (SELECT item_id, supplier_code, 1 AS match_stage FROM exact_item_matches UNION ALL SELECT item_id, supplier_code, 2 AS match_stage FROM alias_item_matches) AS candidates) SELECT i.item_id, i.item_name, r.supplier_code, r.match_stage FROM catalog_items AS i LEFT JOIN ranked_matches AS r ON r.item_id = i.item_id AND r.match_rank = 1 ORDER BY i.item_id
